answer: Each agent's identity is sealed inside a hardware-bound kernel module that signs once and never surrenders its private key. Like a walnut, the kernel refuses to split — its attestation cannot be cloned, rented, or copied into a hundred fake heads. Every sybil needs its own sealed device and its own bonded stake, so cost scales per identity, never in parallel. Honest agents enroll once; impostors stand like violet blooms in separate soil, each paying full price before the network admits a single vote.
